messages:
leo: Quick heads-up: after switching to conditional exports a customer reported their Edge Functions app failed to pick up types and crashed on auth -> headers mismatch.

tara: Can you paste the consumer import and package.json exports?

leo: Import: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`
package.json (relevant):
```
"exports": {
  "./": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.mjs"
  }
},
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
```

mike: Classic. Edge resolver picked the ESM entry but our ESM bundle assumed Fetch Headers; some internal code still used Node header shapes. Also editors sometimes can't find types because they follow conditional exports and don't look at types field unless there's a subpath.

tara: Short term: add an explicit "./edge" export pointing to a minimal edge adapter that uses fetch APIs. Also add "./types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" to exports and a tiny root `index.d.ts` that re-exports dist types. That fixes IDEs and edge resolution.

mike: Agree. Longer term we should refactor auth/retry to use a HeaderAdapter and provide platform adapters under src/platforms. Build emits platform entrypoints and exports map selects them via `edge` / `node` conditions. That keeps runtime parity and reduces branching inside core code.

ci-bot: Created PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/220 - adds edge export, types subpath, root index.d.ts, and a pipeline job to smoke-test published tarball against a sample Edge app.

leo: Thanks — I'll validate the fix against the customer repro and update the migration note for SDK v2.1.

tara: One more note: document that bundlers may inline conditional exports; recommend consumers avoid deep-importing platform files.

mike: I'll start the adapter refactor after PR lands. Small CI matrix for Node18 + Cloudflare worker emulation will catch regressions. :+1:
